title: Choose the visual world for Brett Sabol Plumbing
question: The roll assigned Tested & Tagged. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Tested & Tagged
options.lineage: Backflow test tags and the PA Master Plumber license card
options.thesis: Every page is a signed test tag, so the credentials become the design.
options.viewport: One wide tag hung from a grommet: blue header with the real logo, ruled fields for service, area, license #43391 and backflow, and the phone stamped in red as the call action.
options.risk: Most homeowners never read a backflow tag, and repeating the form grammar everywhere can tip into paperwork.

raised.raise: Picking a problem on the services tag isolates its fields and dims the rest, so a stressed visitor reads one fix at a time.
Brand color lives only in the tag header band and edge binding. Reading fields stay black ink on white stock.
One live mark per screen: the red call stamp is the only lit state, everything else stays ink.
One ruled field grid sets every row, label and photo edge on every page.
Total ground commitment: white tag stock owns every page, no tinted card islands.

options.label: The Truck Side
options.lineage: Brett Sabol's own fleet livery: box truck, van and Kenworth door
options.thesis: The site reads like the side of the truck parked in your driveway.
options.viewport: The truck lettering at billboard scale: logo square, PLUMBING in blue, HEATING & in red, Jet Drain Cleaning, and the black phone number as the call button beside the real van photo.
options.risk: Closest to what a good trades site already does, so it lands familiar. Its strength is that it is literally their brand.

options.label: Endurance Livery
options.lineage: Gulf and Martini racing liveries as identity systems
options.thesis: Brett's blue and red run nose to tail as a stripe system that carries every page.
options.viewport: A blue, red and blue stripe crosses the full width, the license number sits in a race roundel, and services are gridded like sponsor panels.
options.case: Fuses cleanly with the fleet look and wins on recognition, but racing speed is a promise this company never makes, so it loses on clarity.
options.risk: Can read as motorsport costume on a family plumber.

options.label: Event Display
options.thesis: Services as tracks curving out of one event.
options.viewport: A ring section with services as tracks.
options.case: Physics imagery confuses a homeowner mid-emergency. Loses both axes.
options.kept: Select one item to isolate it and dim the rest.

options.label: Iridescent Cloud Edge
options.thesis: Quiet white field with spectral edges.
options.viewport: Wide white margins, color only at hairline edges.
options.case: Pastel atmosphere carries no plumbing truth. Loses both axes.
options.kept: Color confined to band edges while reading text stays achromatic.

options.label: Akari Workshop
options.thesis: Glowing paper volumes in a dim room.
options.viewport: Lit paper moons hung at different heights.
options.case: Warm paper glow says lamp studio, not licensed plumber. Loses both axes.
options.kept: One lit mark per screen as the only live state.

options.label: ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: A text-mode board with numbered exits.
options.viewport: Centered title art over numbered menu lines.
options.case: Terminal nostalgia reads as a tech hobby, not a Bucks County service. Loses both axes.
options.kept: One strict grid governs every element.

options.label: Velvet Mezzotint
options.thesis: Images burnished out of total black.
options.viewport: A dark plate with engraved captions below.
options.case: Velvet gloom fights the white-truck brand. Loses both axes.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A premium plumber site the way the category ships it, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Truck photo under a dark overlay, headline and two buttons at left, a badge row, six service cards below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
